scope: Real native product use cases over disposable PostgreSQL; synthetic publication, actor records and adapter. No configured database, real provider inference or production publication.

server.build: npm run build passed, including production TypeScript and generated assets
server.lint: npm run lint passed; zero errors, three pre-existing warnings outside this stage
server.all_test_sources_typecheck: npx tsc --noEmit retains 30 pre-existing errors in unrelated fixtures; no new NodiaAI, authority or product-log fixture errors

integration.command: npm run test:nodia-ai:products (final build and its three integration scripts executed separately against the same compiled release)

transport.verification: actual Windows stdio subprocess; last registered name, replay, rejected names, cancellation notification, UTF-8 and exact bounds

verified_invariants: All 59 native read ports executed positive SQL cases and validated exact output contracts; five typed families are not only metadata stubs
Actual publication composition selects precisely approved IDs without activating extra candidates; an empty worker retains all eleven M1 entities but instantiates neither reader families nor Redis
Ordinary actors require NodiaAI, destination assignments and existing action requirements; super_admin preserves native transversal authority without impersonation
Finance uses REPEATABLE READ, other families preserve READ COMMITTED; resource revocation remains subject to the native lock and fresh statement protocol
Gateway internal SQL deadline propagates without native barriers widening three seconds to five, and SET/LOCK remains before the first MVCC query
Result schema validation precedes resource-result authorization on replay; membership and session revocation deny stored projections
Core role associations are bounded before ORM hydration; list includes and unbounded all flags are not exposed
Bigint IDs above JavaScript safe integer remain exact strings, financial amounts remain exact, product log identity is UUID, zero/false/null retain their meaning
Five business list queries have unique ID tie-breakers; three disjoint pages of equal-timestamp rows fail before the fix and pass afterward
Provider settings do not claim live availability; credentials, arbitrary fields, messages, event JSON and private relations do not enter public projections
Two worker runs receive the complete 72-tool catalog and use native Business, Finance and Rental callbacks, an external observation with durable replay and a private artifact reference
Transport ceilings are verified and fail explicitly, while argument/result budgets remain unchanged; no generic invoke, arbitrary SQL, URL or model fallback is introduced
External prepare and final verification use short SQL checkpoints; actual native external use cases perform zero SQL during observation and reuse batched selected credentials without N+1 queries
External validated receipts precede I/O and forbid redispatch of incomplete calls; completed replay requires matching current configuration fingerprint and authority without new network calls
Cancellation and absolute deadline are forwarded; late, malformed, revoked or config-changed responses are never published
Human artifact downloads reauthorize chat expiry, owner/super_admin, destination, receipt and resource before and after external I/O; no signed URLs or document/CSV content enter tool results

CSV references regenerate current data at download with row and byte limits and formula protection; invoice object reads enforce declared and actual stream bytes and destroy the stream on errors or cancellation
Artifact references disappear with existing chat/tool-call cascade; no additional persisted files, database tables, migrations or dependencies are introduced
publication_gates: Explicit review/approval of product knowledge and exact bindings, without automatically approving draft documents
Deploy compatible Server and native bridge together and verify these new product tools with the actual Gemini adapter before publishing
Keep the full-stage checklist open for publication and real adapter acceptance; the eight remaining implementation ports are now completed locally
Future tools exceed the measured 72-tool ceiling and require another explicit measured review or bounded selection before publication
Volume, concurrency, deployment, restoration and full production acceptance keep their separate planned checks
